title: traffic-switch-patterns-and-commander-cheatsheet-wip
body:
Purpose:
This is a working cheatsheet for the person who is driving a progressive rollout (the Commander). Focused on traffic switch patterns (manual + semi-automated), quick runbook steps, handoffs, and short scripts to run in emergencies.

Context / problem statement:
- We run a lot of LLM feature launches where cost/latency tradeoffs and behavioral regressions are the main risks.
- Need a small set of reliable traffic-swap patterns that any oncall or product owner can execute without deep infra knowledge.
- This doc is intentionally terse: one page of patterns + safe defaults + scripts.

Quick glossary (Commander language):
- Commander: person executing traffic slice allocations and communicating with stakeholders.
- Slice: a traffic cohort that is routed to variant A or B. Often defined by cookie, header, user-id hash, or region.
- Variant: model version or routing policy being tested.
- Canary: very small live slice used to validate safety signals before ramp.
- Swap: atomically moving traffic from Variant A to Variant B for a slice.

Primary goals for any activation:
- minimize blast radius (cost, latency, hallucination)
- get high-confidence signal quickly for rollback decisions
- keep stakeholders informed with a tight cadence

Safe defaults (use these unless explicitly overridden):
- Initial canary = 0.5% global traffic, 5% internal/staff users if available
- Canary duration = min(30m, 3k reqs) (whichever comes later)
- Ramp steps: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%
- Ramp wait: 30m between small steps, 2h between large steps or until signal clears
- Abort threshold: any critical SLO breach (error rate, p95 latency) or a quality regression > 3 sigma from baseline on monitored prompts

Commander checklist (pre-activation):
- owners and backups listed in release ticket (Jira JIRA-ROLL-78)
- smoke tests passing against the new variant in staging + synthetic traffic job green
- monitoring dash ready: latency, errors, token-cost, quality evals, user complaints feed
- rollback path tested: known-good variant pinned and quick-switch playbook validated
- comms channel open: #prod-rollouts, Pager duty for SRE on standby, stakeholder list on call roster

Traffic switch patterns (concrete)
1) Minimal Canary (safest, manual)
- What: route 0.5% by hash to variant B for real users + 5% internal staff group by header
- When: first pass for behavioral sanity
- How: Console -> traffic-split -> create slice named "canary-<timestamp>" -> set variant B = 0.5% (hash) + header override for staff
- Expected checks during window: p95 latency, errors, top-k hallucination score on eval prompts, UX feedback slack channel
- Abort: immediate if errors > 0.5% or p95 latency +30% over baseline

2) Swap+Hold (fast rollback friendly)
- What: swap traffic for a small slice atomically, hold for X minutes, then either ramp or rollback
- When: when swap codepaths have low infra change but potential model regressions
- How: create named slice -> perform atomic swap command (console button or API) -> start hold timer (recommended 45m)
- Safety: automatic fallback rule that after 60m will revert if no explicit ACK in the console (useful when Commander gets paged)

3) Blue-Green-esque phased swap (operational)
- What: keep both variants live, slowly move cohorts via weighted routing, with final cutover option
- When: heavy infra dependency or stateful caches that require parallel warm-up
- How: weights 5/95 -> 20/80 -> 50/50 -> 0/100, with CV checks at each step

4) Canary + Synthetic Burst (for rare-exit regressions)
- What: run a large synthetic job hitting a specific prompt distribution while canary is live to exercise edge behavior
- When: model changes that affect retrieval, search, or rare tokens
- How: schedule synthetic job to start 10m after canary begins; verify logs and token distribution

Observation checklist (signals to watch)
- Infra: 5xx rate, p95/p99 latency, GPU queue depth, eviction/restart events
- Cost: tokens per response, serving instances scale, sudden token spikes
- Quality: automated eval-sparkline on preselected prompt-suite, new hallucination flag rate, rerank delta (if we have reranker)
- UX: user feedback tags, support tickets with "model output" label, mobile crash rate (if change affects client)

Decision matrix (simple):
- If critical infra SLO breached -> ABORT -> rollback to pinned variant -> page SRE -> start incident pagebook
- If quality regressions (stat sig) -> PAUSE -> increase canary to staff-only cohort for deeper investigation -> run targeted synthetic tests
- If metrics stable across 3 checkpoints -> CONTINUE RAMP per safe defaults

Communication cadence (Commander -> stakeholders)
- T+0 (activation): Slack post to #prod-rollouts (template below)
- T+30m: quick status (green/amber/red) with top-3 signals
- On any abort: immediate Slack + @oncall + short writeup in Jira ticket
- Post-100%: postmortem owner assigned within 48h

Slack activation template (paste and send):
[START] Launching canary for <feature> (ticket JIRA-ROLL-78). Canary slice: 0.5% public + 5% staff. Monitoring: dash/link. SRE oncall: @sre-oncall. Expect updates at +30m, +2h. If critical alerts, we will abort and revert to variant <x>.

Quick rollback commands (examples)
- Console: slice -> edit -> set traffic weight variant A = 100% -> save -> confirm
- API (curl): curl -X POST $CONSOLE/api/v1/slices/<id>/flip -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"target_variant":"stable"}'
- If console unresponsive: route via edge-proxy set-route CLI: redwood route swap --slice <id> --to stable --force

Automated guardrails we recommend enabling for most rollouts:
- auto-revert-on-5xx (threshold 0.5% over baseline for 15m)
- p95-latency-sla (if breached by 40% for 10m, throttle new canary ramps)
- anomaly detection on token cost (alert + hold ramp)

Handoff and escalation protocol (short):
- Commander sets the slice and posts start message. If Commander needs to hand off because of incident, they must: assign a new Commander in ticket, post handoff message with current metric snapshot and last action, and ping SRE.
- If no Commander ACK within 60m, automation reverts slice to pinned variant (safety net).

Post-activation checklist (first 24h):
- Collect: time-series export of main signals, top 20 user conversations for human review, list of errors with stack traces
- Quick triage meeting (30m) with SRE, product, ML, and support within 6h if any amber/red events
- If rollout completed: create postmortem doc stub and assign owner; schedule a 1-week follow-up to check downstream metrics (retention, cost per active session)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we make 0.5% default staff-target mandatory for all model changes? (Pros: early human signal; Cons: leaks to staff analytics)
- Add console quick-button for "staff-only canary" to reduce manual steps
- Standardize synthetic job bundles per model-family (currently ad-hoc)
- Need a sample deck for legal/compliance when private deployments are part of rollout

Links / references (internal):
- activation runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ROLL/activation-runbook
- prelaunch checklist template: CONFLUENCE-6002
- related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412

Handy cheat snippets for the Commander (copyable):
- "Starting canary: canary-{{ts}} — 0.5% public, 5% staff; checks: p95, 5xx, eval-suite"
- "Abort & revert: flipping slice {{id}} -> stable; paging SRE now"
- "Ramping to 10% after green: execute ramp-step --slice {{id}} --to 10 --wait 30m"

Notes (tone, why this is different):
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive. Lots of other artifacts cover theory; this is a quick operational playbook and communication cheat sheet for the person in the hot seat.

If you are the next Commander: read this first, then run through the pre-activation checklist out loud on the channel. Keep the messages short and time-stamped.

-- Lucas
